world.title: Ebola reaches eighth Congo province as Kenya confirms eighth case
world.summary: Kenya confirmed its eighth Ebola infection on Sunday, while the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported cases in an eighth province, North Ubangi, which borders the Central African Republic. Kenya’s latest patient, a 49-year-old hospital attendant, was likely exposed to the country’s first patient, who arrived from C
world.content: Kenya confirmed its eighth Ebola infection on Sunday, while the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported cases in an eighth province, North Ubangi, which borders the Central African Republic. Kenya’s latest patient, a 49-year-old hospital attendant, was likely exposed to the country’s first patient, who arrived from Congo via Uganda and died in Nairobi on Oct. 5. The Bundibugyo-strain outbreak has caused at least 9,400 cases and more than 4,500 deaths in Congo; the latest national tally recorded 9,415 cases and 4,536 deaths through Oct. 16. In Kenya, the seven other people who tested positive include three health workers and a relative of the first patient. The new case was identified after 38 people were tested. Officials say the patients were under quarantine or being monitored through contact tracing and report no evidence of community transmission. In Congo, the two newly recorded North Ubangi cases were men in their 20s, one of whom died. Ituri remains the outbreak’s main focus. Transmission is spreading across a wider area even as some local clusters decline. Health workers face mistrust, population movement and poor access to affected communities. North Kivu is due to restrict entry from Ituri for one week starting Monday, Oct. 19, limit passenger numbers in vehicles and suspend large gatherings.

world.title: Pope Leo plans gradual return to duties after cancer surgery
world.summary: Pope Leo XIV made his first major public appearance since surgery for lung cancer on Sunday, telling about 15,000 people in St. Peter’s Square that he would gradually resume his duties. The 71-year-old pontiff had part of his right lung removed on Oct. 13; the operation confirmed adenocarcinoma, a common form of lung c
world.content: Pope Leo XIV made his first major public appearance since surgery for lung cancer on Sunday, telling about 15,000 people in St. Peter’s Square that he would gradually resume his duties. The 71-year-old pontiff had part of his right lung removed on Oct. 13; the operation confirmed adenocarcinoma, a common form of lung cancer. Leo thanked his supporters and the medical staff at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital and said the experience had brought him closer to people living with illness. He appeared at a window of the Apostolic Palace, led the Angelus prayer and returned to his apartment. Tests on the tumor and nearby lymph nodes are underway. Doctors will use the results, including the tumor’s molecular and genetic profile, to decide whether he needs further treatment. His Nov. 6-17 trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru remains planned; chief thoracic surgeon Stefano Margaritora said he sees no clinical reason it should not proceed.

world.title: Zelensky warns Ukraine cannot withstand US alignment with Russia
world.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Sunday that Ukraine could not prevail if the United States sided with Russia, as Kyiv and Washington gave conflicting accounts of disruptions to satellite communications used by Ukrainian forces. Zelenskyy said U.S. intelligence sharing on Russian ballistic-missile attacks h
world.content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Sunday that Ukraine could not prevail if the United States sided with Russia, as Kyiv and Washington gave conflicting accounts of disruptions to satellite communications used by Ukrainian forces. Zelenskyy said U.S. intelligence sharing on Russian ballistic-missile attacks had resumed after a three-day interruption, but access to SpaceX’s Starlink satellite internet service remained restricted. President Donald Trump denied ordering interference, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio said no one at the White House had directed a slowdown. The dispute follows Trump’s October 11 announcement of an energy ceasefire and pressure on Ukraine to stop strikes on Russian oil facilities. Neither Kyiv nor Moscow confirmed the truce, and both continued attacks. Trump also moved to ease sanctions on Russian diesel exports, saying he wanted to keep Moscow at the negotiating table. Zelenskyy said Russia launched more than 4,000 strike drones, bombs and missiles in the past week, while attacks on energy substations left tens of thousands without electricity. U.S. lawmakers are seeking investigations into the communications disruption: a bipartisan group of senators called for an inspector general review, and Representative Mike Turner demanded a congressional inquiry.

world.title: Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama rejects resignation calls as violent protests enter sixth day
world.summary: Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama refused to resign on Sunday as clashes between police and demonstrators in Tirana entered a sixth day. Protesters are demanding action on poor university conditions, high tuition fees and corruption, as well as Rama’s departure. Police used water cannon, tear gas and rubber bullets afte
world.content: Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama refused to resign on Sunday as clashes between police and demonstrators in Tirana entered a sixth day. Protesters are demanding action on poor university conditions, high tuition fees and corruption, as well as Rama’s departure. Police used water cannon, tear gas and rubber bullets after demonstrators threw rocks and Molotov cocktails. A police station and the entrance to the Interior Ministry were set on fire, and windows were smashed at the governing Socialist Party’s headquarters. Albania’s Health Ministry reported that 272 people had been injured since the protests began Tuesday, including 169 police officers; 12 people were hospitalized after Saturday’s clashes. The European Commission condemned the violence and said authorities must keep their response lawful and proportionate and uphold the right to peaceful protest. Rama called the unrest the “work of an outside hand” and said it threatens Albania’s path to European Union membership, not his government. The student protests followed months of anti-government demonstrations initially sparked by a resort project linked to U.S. President Donald Trump’s family. Rama’s planned visit to Austria on Monday was canceled by the Albanian side.

world.title: Israeli police arrest suspects after settler attacks on diplomats, journalist
world.summary: Israeli police said Monday they had arrested suspects in attacks by settlers on a U.S. photojournalist and European diplomats over the weekend in the occupied West Bank. Reports put the number of arrests at at least eight. Settlers beat Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine as she covered Palestinian olive picking,
world.content: Israeli police said Monday they had arrested suspects in attacks by settlers on a U.S. photojournalist and European diplomats over the weekend in the occupied West Bank. Reports put the number of arrests at at least eight. Settlers beat Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine as she covered Palestinian olive picking, then assaulted a delegation that included Belgian, French and Polish diplomats in Taybeh the next day. The arrests followed international pressure on Israel to prosecute those responsible. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged Israel to crack down on settler violence, and U.S. diplomats visited Taybeh on Sunday. The European Union called for accountability and measures to prevent further attacks on Palestinians and journalists. Police said they detained the suspects for questioning in a pre-dawn operation involving police, military forces and the Shin Bet domestic security service. Investigators cited suspected offenses including violence, violations of a closed military zone order and illegal construction. Police did not publicly identify the suspects.
world.image_alt: Israeli police arrest suspects after settler attacks on diplomats, journalist

world.title: Ukraine
world.summary: Ukraine launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia overnight into Oct. 18 in one of its largest attacks of the war. Russian authorities said air defenses downed 1,015 drones across 15 regions, occupied Crimea and the Black Sea. St. Petersburg Governor Alexander Beglov said strikes started fires at the city’s oil termina
world.content: Ukraine launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia overnight into Oct. 18 in one of its largest attacks of the war. Russian authorities said air defenses downed 1,015 drones across 15 regions, occupied Crimea and the Black Sea. St. Petersburg Governor Alexander Beglov said strikes started fires at the city’s oil terminal and Ruchi depot, killing one person and injuring five. Residential buildings and industrial sites were also damaged. The attack also hit a logistics hub operated by Russian retailer Ozon and a data center run by technology company VK. Ozon said some orders could be canceled as deliveries were rerouted. VK said services remained available, though users reported disruptions. U.S. President Donald Trump has criticized attacks on Russian energy infrastructure and paused new sanctions, saying they could hinder negotiations. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia had continued striking Ukrainian energy sites after Trump announced an energy ceasefire on Oct. 11. He also said U.S.-Ukraine intelligence sharing had resumed after a brief interruption. Zelenskyy later discussed diplomacy with U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.

world.title: Brazil’s Lula and Bolsonaro trade attacks before tight Oct. 25 runoff
world.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, traded insults and accusations in their first televised debate on Sunday, a week before Brazil’s Oct. 25 presidential runoff. The candidates clashed over the economy, crime, health care and corruption. Fl
world.content: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, traded insults and accusations in their first televised debate on Sunday, a week before Brazil’s Oct. 25 presidential runoff. The candidates clashed over the economy, crime, health care and corruption. Flávio Bolsonaro won 47.03% of the first-round vote to Lula’s 45.16%. Lula challenged his opponent over an investigation into financing for a film about his father and called for both candidates to open their personal finances to scrutiny. Brazil’s Federal Police separately asked the Supreme Court to open a money-laundering investigation involving Flávio Bolsonaro and a lawyer close to him; the senator denies wrongdoing. The debate offered few detailed policy proposals, and analysts said the candidates did not use it to reach undecided voters. They are scheduled to meet again on TV Globo on Oct. 23, two days before the vote.

world.title: Austrian Airlines flight diverts to Sofia after bomb threat; checks find no danger
world.summary: An Austrian Airlines Airbus A320 flying from Tel Aviv to Vienna diverted to Sofia on Sunday, Oct. 18, after its crew reported a bomb threat near the Romanian border. A Bulgarian MiG-29 escorted the aircraft to the airport, where 51 passengers and six crew members were safely evacuated. Bulgarian authorities and airline
world.content: An Austrian Airlines Airbus A320 flying from Tel Aviv to Vienna diverted to Sofia on Sunday, Oct. 18, after its crew reported a bomb threat near the Romanian border. A Bulgarian MiG-29 escorted the aircraft to the airport, where 51 passengers and six crew members were safely evacuated. Bulgarian authorities and airline staff searched the plane, passengers and crew. Austrian Airlines said Monday that the checks found no danger. Passengers reboarded, and the flight continued to Vienna. Bulgaria set up a crisis response team and opened an investigation. Haaretz reported that the airline received the warning from an Austrian citizen who was not aboard. Authorities have not publicly identified the person who issued the warning or announced the investigation's findings.

business.title: Meta, Tesla results to test AI spending and market rally
business.summary: Meta and Tesla are among the major companies reporting quarterly results this week as investors assess whether heavy artificial intelligence spending can generate returns and sustain U.S. stock market gains. Both companies are scheduled to report Wednesday. SpaceX is due Tuesday, with Netflix, GE Aerospace, General Mot
business.content: Meta and Tesla are among the major companies reporting quarterly results this week as investors assess whether heavy artificial intelligence spending can generate returns and sustain U.S. stock market gains. Both companies are scheduled to report Wednesday. SpaceX is due Tuesday, with Netflix, GE Aerospace, General Motors and other large companies also reporting this week. Five major technology companies’ combined capital spending could reach about $1.2 trillion next year, according to a Goldman Sachs forecast cited by VG.hu. LSEG IBES data cited by Seeking Alpha forecast third-quarter earnings growth of more than 30% for S&P 500 companies. The Federal Reserve enters its blackout period ahead of its Oct. 27-28 policy meeting.

business.title: Trump faces voter backlash as gasoline costs stay high before midterms
business.summary: President Donald Trump faces voter backlash over gasoline prices, which have approached the average during former President Joe Biden’s term, after making lower energy costs a centerpiece of his 2024 campaign. Voters increasingly link rising energy bills to his administration’s policies. An attack on Iran launched on F
business.content: President Donald Trump faces voter backlash over gasoline prices, which have approached the average during former President Joe Biden’s term, after making lower energy costs a centerpiece of his 2024 campaign. Voters increasingly link rising energy bills to his administration’s policies. An attack on Iran launched on Feb. 28 drove fuel costs higher, according to The Conversation, adding to pressure from grocery and utility bills. Trump has repeatedly said oil prices would “drop like a rock,” but more than half of Americans say they are struggling to afford to fill their tanks, The Conversation reported. Higher fuel prices also affect transport costs: trucks carry more than 70% of U.S. freight, and more than 70% of trucks run on diesel. Fuel costs are a prominent campaign issue ahead of the midterm elections.
business.image_alt: Trump faces voter backlash as gasoline costs stay high before midterms

business.title: AI data-center debt fears rise as CoreWeave bond yields top 15%
business.summary: CoreWeave, an artificial-intelligence data-center operator with 51 centers and $72 billion in debt, faces mounting investor concern. Market pricing put its default risk above 60%, and its bond yields exceeded 15% last week. Its shares fell 24%, including a 12% drop on Oct. 16. CoreWeave pays for chips and long-term fac
business.content: CoreWeave, an artificial-intelligence data-center operator with 51 centers and $72 billion in debt, faces mounting investor concern. Market pricing put its default risk above 60%, and its bond yields exceeded 15% last week. Its shares fell 24%, including a 12% drop on Oct. 16. CoreWeave pays for chips and long-term facility leases before earning revenue from customers and may remain responsible for leases after customers leave. Oracle’s planned 902-megawatt Wisconsin data center has run into grid-approval delays, and Aterio says it is increasingly unlikely to open before 2029.

business.title: Alberta voters decide whether to pursue binding secession referendum
business.summary: Alberta voters are deciding whether the western Canadian province should take legal steps toward a binding referendum on leaving Canada, beginning a process rather than triggering immediate independence. The ballot asks whether Alberta should remain a Canadian province or pursue that next step; any eventual separation
business.content: Alberta voters are deciding whether the western Canadian province should take legal steps toward a binding referendum on leaving Canada, beginning a process rather than triggering immediate independence. The ballot asks whether Alberta should remain a Canadian province or pursue that next step; any eventual separation would require negotiations and constitutional changes. Alberta is central to Canada’s oil and gas economy. Separatists say federal policies disadvantage the energy sector, and some residents feel the province contributes more than it receives. Prime Minister Mark Carney has warned that a separation campaign could deter investment, citing his account of economic uncertainty during Brexit. Alberta’s election authority expects results on the separation question early Tuesday.
business.image_alt: Alberta voters decide whether to pursue binding secession referendum

business.title: Elizabeth Holmes documentary earns $15 million in limited theatrical opening
business.summary: “You Can See Everything,” a documentary about convicted Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, grossed an estimated $15 million in North America during its opening weekend, despite playing in only 855 theaters. Co-directed by comedian Nathan Fielder and filmmaker Lance Oppenheim, the nearly three-hour film had more than 2,
business.content: “You Can See Everything,” a documentary about convicted Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, grossed an estimated $15 million in North America during its opening weekend, despite playing in only 855 theaters. Co-directed by comedian Nathan Fielder and filmmaker Lance Oppenheim, the nearly three-hour film had more than 2,000 sold-out screenings, according to distributor A24 and box-office estimates. The opening was the second-largest for a non-musical documentary, behind Michael Moore’s “Fahrenheit 9/11,” and the biggest for a film playing in fewer than 1,000 theaters since “Borat” opened in 2006. The film follows Holmes and her family in the weeks before she reported to federal prison. It opened in theaters on Oct. 16.
business.image_alt: Elizabeth Holmes documentary earns $15 million in limited theatrical opening

business.title: Gold rises as traders cut October Fed hike bets after Warsh remarks
business.summary: Gold rose on Monday as traders reduced expectations of an October interest-rate increase after remarks by Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh. Spot gold rose 0.3% to $4,175.60 an ounce, and U.S. December futures gained 0.4% to $4,196.40. Lower oil prices also supported bullion by easing inflation concerns. Gold does not
business.content: Gold rose on Monday as traders reduced expectations of an October interest-rate increase after remarks by Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh. Spot gold rose 0.3% to $4,175.60 an ounce, and U.S. December futures gained 0.4% to $4,196.40. Lower oil prices also supported bullion by easing inflation concerns. Gold does not pay interest, so higher borrowing costs can make it less attractive to investors. Traders put the chance of an October hike at 16% and a December increase at 92%, according to CME’s FedWatch Tool. Investors are awaiting next week’s Federal Open Market Committee meeting and U.S. personal consumption expenditures inflation data, which the Fed uses to track its 2% inflation target.
business.image_alt: Gold rises as traders cut October Fed hike bets after Warsh remarks

business.content: Berkshire Hathaway is investing nearly $1 billion in Bending Spoons, a technology company that acquires businesses and emphasizes long-term ownership and learning. Berkshire has historically avoided technology stocks. Warren Buffett retired as Berkshire’s chief executive at the end of 2025 but remains its chairman, according to an account of the company’s past investments.

business.title: Microsoft exits Nscale
business.summary: Microsoft has ended its agreement to lease capacity at British AI infrastructure company Nscale’s planned data center in Loughton, Essex, after delays to the site’s electricity connection pushed the expected supply date into the 2030s. Nscale announced the project in 2025 with a £2 billion commitment. It had been due t
business.content: Microsoft has ended its agreement to lease capacity at British AI infrastructure company Nscale’s planned data center in Loughton, Essex, after delays to the site’s electricity connection pushed the expected supply date into the 2030s. Nscale announced the project in 2025 with a £2 billion commitment. It had been due to open next year, and Microsoft had planned to fund a supercomputer there. The withdrawal leaves Nscale without a publicly announced customer for the Essex site. The company says it remains committed to the project and is examining alternative power sources. UK Power Networks, which operates the regional electricity grid, told Nscale it could not provide enough power until the early to mid-2030s. Nscale says the grid delay does not affect its other contracts and that it continues to work with Microsoft on projects in Norway, Portugal and the United States.

science.title: Norwegian study links longer breastfeeding with fewer childhood ADHD symptoms
science.summary: A Norwegian study of 37,643 children found that longer periods of full breastfeeding were associated with fewer attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms at ages 3, 5 and 8. The research, led by University of Bergen psychiatrist Berit Skretting Solberg, was published in Biological Psychiatry. The associa
science.content: A Norwegian study of 37,643 children found that longer periods of full breastfeeding were associated with fewer attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms at ages 3, 5 and 8. The research, led by University of Bergen psychiatrist Berit Skretting Solberg, was published in Biological Psychiatry. The association persisted after researchers accounted for children’s and parents’ genetic ADHD risk and other family and birth-related factors. However, the observational study measured symptoms through parent questionnaires and cannot establish that breastfeeding caused the difference. The authors said the effect on individual children was small.
science.image_alt: Norwegian study links longer breastfeeding with fewer childhood ADHD symptoms

science.title: Researchers propose hybrid quantum computer to cut simulation demands
science.summary: A team led by Eleanor Crane, a quantum computing lecturer at King’s College London, has proposed a theoretical design that combines superconducting qubits with microwave cavity resonators to simulate systems involving both fermions and bosons. The researchers say the approach could reduce the hardware and gate requirem
science.content: A team led by Eleanor Crane, a quantum computing lecturer at King’s College London, has proposed a theoretical design that combines superconducting qubits with microwave cavity resonators to simulate systems involving both fermions and bosons. The researchers say the approach could reduce the hardware and gate requirements that make boson simulations difficult on conventional qubit-only machines. The researchers tested the framework using models of a beam splitter and simplified quantum systems, including a (2+1)-dimensional gauge model. They estimate it could reduce computational work a thousandfold and make some chemistry and materials simulations feasible on near-term devices. The proposal has been published in *Physical Review X*.
science.image_alt: Researchers propose hybrid quantum computer to cut simulation demands

science.content: SpaceX was scheduled to launch its Bandwagon-5 rideshare mission Monday morning with the Starfall reentry capsule and 31 customer payloads, according to Spaceflight Now’s live coverage. science.title: El Niño drought pushes India to import sugar, lifting global prices
science.summary: El Niño-linked drought and India's weakest monsoon in 11 years have damaged sugarcane crops, prompting the world's second-largest sugar producer to open its market to imports as prices rise in India and globally. India is also the world's largest sugar consumer, and shortages have hit during the Hindu festival season,
science.content: El Niño-linked drought and India's weakest monsoon in 11 years have damaged sugarcane crops, prompting the world's second-largest sugar producer to open its market to imports as prices rise in India and globally. India is also the world's largest sugar consumer, and shortages have hit during the Hindu festival season, when demand for sweets is high. Sugarcane supplies India's ethanol fuel program, which has made a 20% ethanol blend the standard at petrol stations and provides sugar mills with an additional source of revenue. Reduced cane availability complicates efforts to cut oil imports. Protests have erupted over rising prices, and the government has warned traders against speculative stockpiling.
science.image_alt: El Niño drought pushes India to import sugar, lifting global prices

science.title: Astronomers model first green white dwarf from planetary debris
science.summary: Astronomers led by Mark Hollands, an astrophysicist at the University of Warwick, have identified a white dwarf whose light would appear green to human eyes. The object, WD J1330+6435, has a temperature of about 4,000 degrees Celsius and has accumulated rocky material containing sodium, calcium and lithium. Sodium abso
science.content: Astronomers led by Mark Hollands, an astrophysicist at the University of Warwick, have identified a white dwarf whose light would appear green to human eyes. The object, WD J1330+6435, has a temperature of about 4,000 degrees Celsius and has accumulated rocky material containing sodium, calcium and lithium. Sodium absorbs orange wavelengths, giving the star a greenish appearance in the researchers’ calculations. The researchers did not observe the star’s color directly. They calculated how its recorded spectrum would appear using a model of human color vision. In a sample of 151 white dwarfs within about 65 light-years of Earth, five had unusual modeled colors. The researchers say forthcoming spectroscopic surveys should provide many more stars to examine, and Hollands plans to continue the analysis.
science.image_alt: Astronomers model first green white dwarf from planetary debris

science.title: UK forecast suggests clearer skies for Wednesday’s Orionid meteor peak
science.summary: UK forecasters expect rain to move away early Wednesday night, with clear spells possible during the Orionid meteor shower’s peak. The annual display occurs as Earth passes through dust left by Halley’s Comet; the peak is expected overnight from Oct. 21 to 22. The waxing gibbous Moon may obscure fainter meteors, while
science.content: UK forecasters expect rain to move away early Wednesday night, with clear spells possible during the Orionid meteor shower’s peak. The annual display occurs as Earth passes through dust left by Halley’s Comet; the peak is expected overnight from Oct. 21 to 22. The waxing gibbous Moon may obscure fainter meteors, while brighter ones should remain visible from dark sites. In Mexico, the peak is forecast around midday on Oct. 21, making the pre-dawn hours of Oct. 22 the main viewing opportunity. The National Institute of Astrophysics, Optics and Electronics estimates about 15 meteors an hour, depending on sky conditions.
science.image_alt: UK forecast suggests clearer skies for Wednesday’s Orionid meteor peak

science.title: Japan sets Tuesday launch for first Phobos sample-return mission
science.summary: Japan’s Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) spacecraft is scheduled to launch aboard an H3 rocket from Tanegashima Space Center at 4:41 a.m. Tuesday, Oct. 20, Japan time, beginning a mission to collect material from Phobos and bring it back to Earth. The launch is scheduled for Monday evening UTC; the mission has not yet l
science.content: Japan’s Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) spacecraft is scheduled to launch aboard an H3 rocket from Tanegashima Space Center at 4:41 a.m. Tuesday, Oct. 20, Japan time, beginning a mission to collect material from Phobos and bring it back to Earth. The launch is scheduled for Monday evening UTC; the mission has not yet lifted off. Led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), the mission is designed to make the first round trip to the Martian system and return a sample from one of Mars’ moons. Scientists aim to determine whether Phobos and Deimos formed from debris left by a large impact on Mars or are captured asteroids. The answer could shed light on the moons’ composition and Mars’ history. The spacecraft is expected to reach Mars in August 2027, survey Phobos for about three years and return a sample capsule in 2031. A French-German rover, Idefix, is due to examine Phobos before the spacecraft attempts to collect at least 10 grams of material.
science.image_alt: Japan sets Tuesday launch for first Phobos sample-return mission

sports.title: Cardinals beat Rams on last-second field goal in NFL Week 6
sports.summary: Arizona Cardinals kicker Chad Ryland made a career-high six field goals, including the game-winner as time expired, in an 18-16 upset of the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday. The loss left the preseason Super Bowl favorites at 2-4 and last in the NFC West. The Carolina Panthers beat the Philadelphia Eagles 25-14, extending P
sports.content: Arizona Cardinals kicker Chad Ryland made a career-high six field goals, including the game-winner as time expired, in an 18-16 upset of the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday. The loss left the preseason Super Bowl favorites at 2-4 and last in the NFC West. The Carolina Panthers beat the Philadelphia Eagles 25-14, extending Philadelphia’s losing streak to four games. Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is on injured reserve and will miss at least four weeks. The Houston Texans edged the Jacksonville Jaguars 34-31 in London, while the Cleveland Browns beat the Baltimore Ravens 13-10 on a last-play field goal. Pittsburgh rallied from a 13-point fourth-quarter deficit to defeat Tampa Bay 26-19 in overtime. Week 6 concludes Monday night, when the San Francisco 49ers host the Washington Commanders.
sports.image_alt: Cardinals beat Rams on last-second field goal in NFL Week 6

sports.title: Giants lose 34-27 as McCarthy rallies, Skattebo gets no touches
sports.summary: The New York Giants lost 34-27 to the New Orleans Saints on Oct. 18 in East Rutherford. Running back Cam Skattebo played six snaps and finished without a carry or target for the first time in his career. Skattebo said he understood his reduced role after fumbling in overtime the previous week. Head coach John Harbaugh
sports.content: The New York Giants lost 34-27 to the New Orleans Saints on Oct. 18 in East Rutherford. Running back Cam Skattebo played six snaps and finished without a carry or target for the first time in his career. Skattebo said he understood his reduced role after fumbling in overtime the previous week. Head coach John Harbaugh denied benching him, saying the lack of touches was not by design and that no runs were called while Skattebo was on the field. The Saints built a 34-10 lead before J.J. McCarthy replaced Giants quarterback Jameis Winston early in the fourth quarter. McCarthy threw for 243 yards and led three scoring drives in just over 11 minutes. New York pulled within seven, but McCarthy’s final fourth-down pass into the end zone fell incomplete. Harbaugh said no decision had been made on the starting quarterback for the Giants’ next game, at Houston on Oct. 25. Skattebo said he would prepare for a reduced role unless told otherwise.
sports.image_alt: Giants lose 34-27 as McCarthy rallies, Skattebo gets no touches

sports.title: Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez undergoes jaw surgery, targets return in weeks
sports.summary: Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez underwent successful surgery for a fractured jaw after colliding with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite during Chelsea’s 2-0 Premier League win on Saturday. Martinez was taken to hospital after several minutes of treatment on the pitch and said he hopes to return “in a few weeks”;
sports.content: Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez underwent successful surgery for a fractured jaw after colliding with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite during Chelsea’s 2-0 Premier League win on Saturday. Martinez was taken to hospital after several minutes of treatment on the pitch and said he hopes to return “in a few weeks”; Chelsea have not announced a firm recovery timetable. The injury leaves 21-year-old Belgian goalkeeper Mike Penders in line to deputise after making his Premier League debut as a substitute at Everton. Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso said the club trusts Penders. Martinez could miss upcoming fixtures against Tottenham, Liverpool in the League Cup and Manchester United.
sports.image_alt: Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez undergoes jaw surgery, targets return in weeks

sports.title: Brighton beat Palace 5-0 as Gómez’s 51-metre strike helps lift them to third
sports.summary: Brighton & Hove Albion beat Crystal Palace 5-0 at the Amex Stadium on Sunday, scoring three times in the opening 10 minutes, including Diego Gómez’s 51-metre shot from just inside Palace’s half. Jaydee Canvot’s own goal opened the scoring in the fourth minute; Gómez struck three minutes later, Yasin Ayari made it 3-0,
sports.content: Brighton & Hove Albion beat Crystal Palace 5-0 at the Amex Stadium on Sunday, scoring three times in the opening 10 minutes, including Diego Gómez’s 51-metre shot from just inside Palace’s half. Jaydee Canvot’s own goal opened the scoring in the fourth minute; Gómez struck three minutes later, Yasin Ayari made it 3-0, and Charalampos Kostoulas and Jack Hinshelwood added second-half goals. The win put Brighton third with 16 points after seven Premier League matches, during which they have scored a league-high 23 goals. Crystal Palace, who have conceded more league goals than any other side this season, suffered their fourth defeat in seven matches. Manager Pierre Sage apologized to supporters and said he did not know whether he would be given time to fix the defence. Brighton next visit Jablonec in the Conference League on October 22, then Liverpool in the Premier League on October 25. The Liverpool game begins a run of five away matches.

sports.content: Chelsea beat Tottenham 6-2 at Stamford Bridge on Sunday, with Lauren James and Ellie Carpenter each scoring twice, while Manchester City maintained their perfect Women’s Super League start with a 3-2 win over Brighton. City remain two points ahead of Chelsea, who have won five league games in a row. Chelsea and Tottenham were level at half-time after Matilda Vinberg headed Tottenham’s equaliser, but Carpenter and James scored soon after the break before substitutes Sjoeke Nüsken and Maika Hamano added goals. Chelsea coach Sonia Bompastor said her substitutes came on with confidence and a clear understanding of their roles.

sports.content: Arizona Cardinals kicker Chad Ryland made a 43-yard field goal as time expired Sunday to beat the Los Angeles Rams 18-16 at SoFi Stadium, completing a rally without a touchdown. The result dropped the Rams, who began the season as Super Bowl favorites, to 2-4 and gave Arizona its first win since the season opener. The Rams took a 16-15 lead with 47 seconds left after Matthew Stafford’s five-yard touchdown pass to Colby Parkinson and an extra point by punter Ethan Evans. Evans took over kicking duties after Rams kicker Blake Grupe injured his knee making a tackle. Arizona then moved into range on a 21-yard catch by Jalen Brooks and a 15-yard unnecessary-roughness penalty against Rams cornerback Josh Wallace before Ryland’s sixth field goal won the game. The loss leaves Los Angeles last in the NFC West. Arizona’s defense held the Rams to 286 yards. The Rams visit the Las Vegas Raiders next Sunday, Oct. 25; Arizona hosts the Denver Broncos that day.

sports.content: Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter of the team’s Oct. 18 game against the Las Vegas Raiders after drawing an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for spitting toward Raiders tight end Brock Bowers. Buffalo won 33-30 to improve to 5-1; Las Vegas fell to 3-3. The resulting penalty cost Buffalo 14 yards with 19 seconds left before halftime, helping set up a 27-yard field goal by Las Vegas kicker Matt Gay that tied the game 13-13 at the break. Gardner-Johnson apologized afterward, saying he let his emotions get the better of him and hurt his team. Buffalo head coach Joe Brady said he would address the lack of discipline and that the conduct “can't happen”. Gardner-Johnson expects a fine, and the NFL could review the incident for further discipline, including a suspension.

sports.content: Northampton Saints beat Cardiff 28-12 at Franklin’s Gardens on Sunday, becoming the only English Gallagher Premiership side to win in the opening round of the Investec Champions Cup. Gloucester drew with defending champions Bordeaux-Bègles, while six other English clubs lost. Northampton led 14-0 at half-time before tries from Cardiff’s Harri Millard and Mason Grady cut the gap to two points. George Hendy then scored and chased down Josh Adams to prevent a likely Cardiff try. Fraser Dingwall crossed late to seal the win. Cardiff had rotated players because they faced a five-day turnaround before a United Rugby Championship match against the Sharks. Northampton’s next pool fixtures are in France in December and January; Cardiff host Bath in December.
